types.definition: An explicitly represented event, occasion, appointment or activity serving as content or an argument of the request: something scheduled, recalled, queried, reported, used as a condition or temporal anchor, or included in requested message/list content. A command merely specifying the assistant operation does not by itself supply this role. Apply request-relevant scope.
thinking_requirements: Separate the assistant operation from the event content it operates on. Turn off the lights alone does not express an additional event argument; remind me to turn off the lights does, because turning off is the reminder content.

Accept event nouns, descriptive labels and clauses representing activities or occurrences. A proper event name, concrete participant identity, exact time, or normalized executable value is not required.

An explicitly referenced event category or unresolved instance such as meetings, my next appointment or that event can count. A request to create an empty calendar event still explicitly names the event category; do not invent an event from a date alone.

An asserted or queried occurrence can count when it contributes to the request, including past events, a described assassination, a scheduled arrival/departure, or sunshine during a specified period. Generic object properties, static personal attributes and content-category words alone are not events.
Explicitly postponed, canceled, denied, hypothetical or conditional events remain expressed events. This predicate reports presence, not occurrence truth, commitment, completion or environment state.

An event in requested message content or task-list content counts independently of the native intent. A bare request to send, play, search, switch or schedule without separately expressed event content does not gain event presence merely from that operation verb.

A holiday, birthday or anniversary can be an occasion. A screening or concert can be an event while a film/song title alone is not. Meal/sport/person types may also hold when their own roles are expressed.
Background events count only when they constrain, describe or motivate the requested operation, or are themselves communicated by the request. Unrelated background is outside request-relevant scope.

Where a fragment does not establish whether a word is an event, a title, a person, or another argument, keep the predicate unavailable; neither native annotation nor normally required parameters settle it.
